question.text: \[ \mathbf{x}' = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}\mathbf{x}, \qquad \mathbf{x}_1(t) = \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} e^{-2t}, \quad \mathbf{x}_2(t) = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} e^{2t} \] Consider the system of linear ODEs and two of its linearly independent solutions $\mathbf x_1$ and $\mathbf x_2,$ shown above. Which of the following is a fundamental matrix for the system?
question.explanation:
Given a linear system $\mathbf{x}' = A \mathbf{x},$ where $A$ is an $n \times n$ matrix, a fundamental matrix $\Phi(t)$ of the system is an $n \times n$ matrix whose columns are linearly independent solutions of the system.

In our cases, we have a $2 \times 2$ system. We are also given that the two linearly independent solutions of the system are the following:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{x}_1(t) &= \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} e^{-2t} = \begin{bmatrix} -e^{-2t} \\ e^{-2t} \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \mathbf{x}_2(t) &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} e^{2t} = \begin{bmatrix} 3e^{2t} \\ e^{2t} \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Therefore, our fundamental could be written as \[ \Phi(t) = \begin{bmatrix} -e^{-2t} & 3e^{2t} \\ e^{-2t} & e^{2t} \end{bmatrix}. \]

Note: The columns of $\Phi$ can be written in any order.
